exhibitors.name: 11 Yard Line Collectors
exhibitors.tagline: Breaking live to a room of 2,000.
exhibitors.summary: A Whatnot breaker and card seller with a following over 2,000.
exhibitors.editorial: 11 Yard Line have built an audience of well over two thousand and run their breaks through Whatnot, which makes the RazMania table the in-person version of something they usually do to a live room. Worth a stop if you have only ever bought from them through a screen.

exhibitors.name: 614 Rips
exhibitors.tagline: Where sneaker culture and cardboard meet in Columbus.
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade. Premium trading cards, sold from inside 614Sneaker on North High Street.
sections_html:
Cardboard × sneaker culture

614 Rips runs its card counter inside 614Sneaker on North High Street — putting sports cards, Pokémon and sneaker collectors under one roof. It is the only table on the RazMania floor built that way.

Got cards to sell?

614 Rips is buying at RazMania. Bring the cards you have been meaning to move — they make offers at the table.

✓Sports cards✓Pokémon✓Slabs✓Raw✓Full collections

Something large? Message them before the event so they arrive prepared.

DM 614 Rips →

✦ RazMania Editorial

Why they’re on our radar

614 Rips sits at an intersection we like: sneakers, sports cards and Pokémon, sold from the same counter.

What caught our attention was not the inventory list. In July they built out a proper display case inside the shop to show slabs and singles the way a card store should, and collectors started bringing them real collections.

A collector drove in from Indiana this summer to sell them an entire vintage Pokémon collection. That is the kind of trust you do not manufacture.

They are on the show circuit most weekends, and they are buying at this one.

Brick & mortarCard counter inside 614Sneaker on North High Street, Columbus — not a pop-up.
On the show circuitTravelling to card shows most weekends; new pop-up banner built for the run.
Active buyerBought a full vintage Pokémon collection off a collector who drove in from Indiana.
What they’re known for🏀 Modern sports — rookies, patches, numbered⚡ Pokémon — vintage to modern, raw & graded💎 Slabs & singles — $5 pickups to showcase cards🤝 Buying — offers made at the table

What to look for at their table

In the case nowOhtani Highlight Reel /50 & Cooper Flagg rookie patch$450Flagg: ask at tableAsk them to hold it →From the July collection buyVintage Pokémon, raw and gradedAsk at tableAsk them to hold it →In-case at the showSports & Pokémon singles, slabs and rawFrom $5Ask them to hold it →

Inventory changes constantly. See something you want? DM @614rips before the show and ask them to hold it.

take: Columbus-based, operating out of 614Sneaker on North High Street — trading cards sitting inside a sneaker shop.
An unusual crossover, and a reminder that the pop-culture side of this floor is not an afterthought.

exhibitors.name: ABC Vintage
exhibitors.tagline: A vintage shop with real opening hours.
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade — open Monday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm.
exhibitors.editorial: ABC Vintage keep a shop open Monday to Saturday, 11 to 5, and they have built the largest Instagram following of anyone on this floor by some distance. Vintage is the specialism, and the hours mean you can go back after the show.

exhibitors.name: ABJ Cards
exhibitors.summary: Aaron Ball Jr., buying strong out of Des Moines — sell him anything $20 and up.
exhibitors.editorial: ABJ is Aaron Ball Jr., and the pitch is refreshingly blunt: paying strong, sell me everything twenty dollars and up. He travels in from Des Moines, one of the further-flung buyers on this floor, and a sensible first stop if you arrived carrying rather than browsing.

exhibitors.name: All In Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards, in from Michigan.
exhibitors.editorial: All In Sports Cards take table 239. A newer name on the circuit — the brand is still being built, so the case is the first proper look anyone gets.

exhibitors.name: Atomic TCG
exhibitors.tagline: The biggest following on the floor.
exhibitors.summary: Sean's Pokémon vending operation — 28,000 following, and he films and edits every video himself.
exhibitors.editorial: Atomic is Sean, a Pokémon vendor with 28,000 following on Instagram — the largest audience of anyone exhibiting at RazMania — built across 375 posts he films and edits himself. He publishes his vending schedule publicly, which is how you know the table is a fixture rather than a one-off.

exhibitors.name: Backyard Cards MI
exhibitors.summary: Sports card collecting out of Michigan — buying, selling and trading, with a soft spot for Detroit teams.
exhibitors.editorial: Backyard collect and trade Michigan sports with a particular eye on Detroit teams — a local table for local collectors. If you are chasing Lions, Tigers, Pistons or Red Wings rather than national stars, this is the sort of case that rewards a proper dig.
take: Michigan-based and focused on local and Detroit teams.
A newer operation, which on a show floor often means keener pricing and more willingness to deal.

exhibitors.name: Bad Boyz Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell and trade sports cards — Jordan, Kobe, LeBron and Brady, vintage and modern.
exhibitors.editorial: Bad Boyz deal in the names everyone knows — Jordan, Kobe, LeBron and Brady — across vintage and modern, with nearly 3,000 following and a phone number right in the bio for anyone who wants to talk before the show. If you are hunting one specific icon rather than browsing, start here.

exhibitors.name: Bala Sports
exhibitors.editorial: Bala Sports bring a sports table to both days.

exhibitors.name: Bank Of Cardz
exhibitors.summary: Lansing and West Bloomfield — Michigan cards, bought and sold.
exhibitors.editorial: Bank Of Cardz work out of Lansing and West Bloomfield with close to 700 following. A Michigan operation running on both sides of the state, which usually means inventory that has passed through a lot of hands before it reaches a table.

exhibitors.name: Batter Up Breaks
exhibitors.summary: Baseball, football, hockey and basketball card breaks.
exhibitors.editorial: Batter Up run breaks across baseball, football, hockey and basketball, so whatever you collect there is a slot with your name on it. Breaks are also the cheapest way into a product you would never buy a full box of, which makes them a good first stop for anyone new to the floor.

exhibitors.name: Benchmark Card Co.
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade — premium cards, and they answer every DM.
exhibitors.editorial: Benchmark lead with a promise most dealers would not put in writing: they answer every DM. If you want something specific put aside before the doors open, that is an invitation worth taking them up on.

exhibitors.name: Bridgeport Hobby
exhibitors.tagline: Four blocks from White Sox Park.
exhibitors.summary: Cards, content and breaks from a shop four blocks from White Sox Park — always buying grails, singles and slabs.
exhibitors.editorial: Bridgeport carry the largest following of anyone on this floor — 17,000 on Instagram and another 45,000 on TikTok — run out of a shop four blocks from White Sox Park. Cards, content and breaks, with a standing interest in buying grails, singles and slabs.
take: The biggest social following on the floor by a distance — 17,000 on Instagram and another 45,000 on TikTok — run out of a shop four blocks from Sox Park in Chicago.
They post that they are always buying grails, singles and slabs. Travelling this far for a Michigan show usually means bringing inventory worth the trip.

exhibitors.name: Buddy Breaks
exhibitors.summary: Sports card breaks — football, baseball and basketball.
exhibitors.editorial: Buddy Breaks take tables 202 and 203, running sports card breaks across football, baseball and basketball. A two-table footprint dedicated to opening product rather than selling singles.

exhibitors.name: CaptainCards
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards.
exhibitors.editorial: CaptainCards take table 74, a single sports card pitch. One of the smaller footprints on the floor, which usually means a tighter, more selective case rather than long boxes to dig through.
take: Exhibiting at RazMania. Their Instagram presence is minimal, so we have not seen enough public activity to write a fuller view.
Worth walking past rather than planning around — plenty of good tables keep no social footprint at all.

exhibitors.name: Cards HQ
exhibitors.tagline: Atlanta's card superstore, coming to Lake Orion.
exhibitors.summary: The Atlanta card retailer opening a Detroit-area store at Baldwin Commons in Lake Orion.
exhibitors.editorial: CardsHQ built their name in Atlanta on a showcase-led store rather than a stall, and they are opening a Detroit-area location at Baldwin Commons in Lake Orion. Sports cards, Pokémon, boxes and supplies — worth meeting before the local doors open.

exhibitors.name: CBS SportsCards
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards and memorabilia, with an eBay storefront behind the table.
exhibitors.editorial: CBS deal in sports cards and memorabilia, with an eBay storefront and a Discord where the buying, selling and trading carries on between shows. The Discord is the tell — dealers who run one tend to keep talking to their customers long after the tables come down.

exhibitors.name: Cole Street Collision
exhibitors.summary: A Birmingham auto body shop — full collision, paint and 24-hour towing.
exhibitors.editorial: Cole Street is Ron Karmo's shop on Cole Street in Birmingham, open since 2014 and carrying a 4.8 rating across 120 reviews. Full collision and paint work, a certified mechanic on site, 24-hour towing, and they deal with any insurer. Backing RazMania as a partner rather than selling cards.

exhibitors.name: Come Play Detroit
exhibitors.summary: Detroit's largest provider of recreational sports leagues for adults.
exhibitors.editorial: Come Play Detroit run the largest adult recreational sports leagues in the city. A RazMania partner rather than a card dealer — the table to visit if the sport itself appeals more than the cardboard.

exhibitors.name: D&G Sportzcardz
exhibitors.summary: Always buying — DM pictures with prices.
exhibitors.editorial: D&G lead with the shortest pitch on the floor: always buying, send pictures with prices. They run an eBay store under the same name, so if you are bringing cards to sell rather than to browse, start here.

exhibitors.name: D-Town Rips
exhibitors.summary: A Detroit-area dealer and breaker.
exhibitors.editorial: D-Town Rips hold three tables, 86 through 88, and the name states the business — rips, out of the Detroit area. Three tables is a lot of product to work through in two days.

exhibitors.name: Dan-Good Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: Dan-Good Collectibles take table 190, in the back block.

exhibitors.name: DeckTradr
exhibitors.summary: A trading platform for card collectors — trade rather than sell.
exhibitors.editorial: DeckTradr run a trading platform for card collectors, and several dealers on this floor are already affiliates — Pirate Hunter Deegs among them. Worth a conversation if you would rather trade your way up than sell and rebuy.

exhibitors.name: Detroit Card House
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell and trade across soccer, basketball, rugby and baseball.
exhibitors.editorial: Detroit Card House buy, sell and trade across soccer, basketball, rugby and baseball, a wider spread than most tables on this floor. Recent finds include a 2018 Topps Chrome Update Shohei Ohtani International Affair, which tells you the kind of card that turns up in their case.

exhibitors.name: Detroit Legends Sports
exhibitors.tagline: A card shop with a storefront and a Discord.
exhibitors.summary: A local card shop at 55226 Van Dyke, Shelby Twp — buy, sell, trade, with a Discord community attached.
exhibitors.editorial: Detroit Legends run a proper local card shop on Van Dyke in Shelby Township, and they keep a Discord going between shows. That combination of a storefront and a community is rarer than it should be.
take: A bricks-and-mortar shop in Shelby Township that brings a store's depth to a show table — 527 posts and 2,400 followers deep, with buy, sell and trade all advertised equally.
If you are bringing a collection to sell rather than a want list to fill, a dealer with a real storefront behind them is usually the easier conversation.

exhibitors.name: Detroit Sports Cards
exhibitors.editorial: Detroit Sports Cards bring a Detroit-focused sports card table to both days.

exhibitors.name: Diesel's Dugout
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell and trade sports cards out of Waterford, MI and shows across the state. Slabs, singles and mystery bags.
exhibitors.editorial: Diesel's works Waterford and shows across Michigan, and the line they lead with is that they are always buying collections. Bring what you have been meaning to move.
take: Waterford-based, working shows across Michigan, with slabs, singles and mystery bags.
Advertises buying collections outright. Worth a conversation if you are clearing a box rather than filling a binder.

exhibitors.name: DJsportscards
exhibitors.summary: Dylan and Jesse Heber. Always looking to buy, sell and trade.
take: A father-and-son operation with an active eBay storefront and 2,200 followers.
Sellers with a running eBay history price against comps rather than against hope, which usually makes for a faster negotiation.

exhibitors.name: DNA Packs
exhibitors.summary: Football, basketball and baseball, in from West Virginia.
exhibitors.editorial: DNA Packs cover football, basketball and baseball and travel in from West Virginia, which is a long way to bring a table. They buy as readily as they sell — DM us to sell your cards is the standing line.

exhibitors.name: Doc and Treyday
exhibitors.summary: A father-and-son table — Larry, an old army medic, and his son Trey.
exhibitors.editorial: Doc is Larry, an old army medic — hence the name — and Treyday is his son. They run the table together and do Whatnot shows between events, 300 posts into a lifelong collecting habit. One of the few tables here where the story behind it is the point.

exhibitors.name: DoublePull Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: DoublePull Collectibles bring a collectibles table to both days.

exhibitors.name: DrCollectsTCG
exhibitors.summary: One Piece and Riftbound out of Michigan — buy, sell, trade.
exhibitors.editorial: Doctor Collects is one of the few tables leaning into One Piece and Riftbound rather than the usual Pokémon-and-sports split. Michigan based, buying, selling and trading, and worth finding if those are the games you actually play.

exhibitors.name: Dubs Vault TCG
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade, collect.
exhibitors.editorial: Dubs Vault keep the pitch to four words — buy, sell, trade, collect. A newer TCG table, which often means keener pricing than the established shops.

exhibitors.name: Dude Digz
exhibitors.summary: Michigan card vendor — football, basketball and Disney, plus host of the GOAT Debates.
exhibitors.editorial: Dude Digz cover football, basketball and Disney out of Michigan, and host GOAT Debates and fighting-game tournaments alongside the cards. A Justin Jefferson Steampunk one-of-one colour match has already been through their hands, and they only started vending this year.
take: Michigan vendor covering football, basketball and Disney, and a tournament host on the side.
The Disney run is the unusual part — almost nobody else on this floor carries it.

exhibitors.name: Epik Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: Epik Collectibles run a small collectibles table. Worth noting the spelling: their Instagram is @epikcollectibles, with a k, though the exhibitor list has them as Epic.

exhibitors.name: ExoticTCG
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon — always buying, selling and trading.
exhibitors.editorial: Exotic keep it simple: Pokémon, bought, sold and traded, with no sideline in anything else. Single-category dealers tend to carry deeper boxes than the generalists do, so if Pokémon is what you came for, this is a sensible first stop.

exhibitors.name: Fat Katz
exhibitors.tagline: Cards, Hot Wheels and a kids' trade day.
exhibitors.summary: A St. Clair Shores shop — sports cards, Pokémon, Magic and Yu-Gi-Oh, plus vintage Hot Wheels and coins.
exhibitors.editorial: Fat Katz have a shop on Harper Avenue in St. Clair Shores rated 4.8 across 160 reviews, and a range wider than most — sports cards, Pokémon, Magic and Yu-Gi-Oh alongside Hot Wheels going back to the sixties and gold and silver coins. They also run trade days where kids trade with each other, which says plenty about how the table gets run.

exhibitors.name: FireRips
exhibitors.summary: Sports card breaks, live on TikTok.
exhibitors.editorial: Fire Rips run sports card breaks live on TikTok to an audience of nearly 2,500, and bring the same operation to the table in person. If you have only ever watched a break through a screen, this is the one to stand in front of.

exhibitors.name: Fodder TCG
exhibitors.summary: Lucario collector turned Michigan-based vendor, also handling Whatnot consignment.
exhibitors.editorial: A Lucario collector who turned the habit into a business, now vending in Michigan and handling Whatnot consignment. Collector-turned-dealer tables are usually the ones where you can talk about a card for ten minutes rather than just buy it.
take: Michigan TCG vendor and a Lucario collector, which tells you where the specialist knowledge sits.
Small table, specific expertise. Ask them about the thing they actually collect.

exhibitors.name: Game Time Hobby Shop
exhibitors.tagline: Retro games and cards under one roof.
exhibitors.summary: Retro games, sports cards, Pokémon and TCG — a shop that buys and trades daily.
exhibitors.editorial: GameTime run a bricks-and-mortar shop combining retro video games with sports cards, Pokémon and TCG, open every day and buying and trading daily, with nearly 10,000 following. The games-and-cards crossover is rare on this floor.

exhibitors.name: GemMint.com
exhibitors.tagline: One of the country's biggest PSA submission groups.
exhibitors.summary: One of the largest PSA card grading submission groups in the country.
exhibitors.editorial: GemMint run one of the largest PSA grading submission groups in the country, with a support line on 833-520-0005. They work the convention circuit, Collect-A-Con included, and are at RazMania to take submissions rather than to sell you singles.

exhibitors.name: Global Soccer
exhibitors.editorial: Global Soccer bring a soccer-focused table to both days.

exhibitors.name: Good Karma Cards
exhibitors.summary: Kindness is global.
exhibitors.editorial: Good Karma trade under a two-word philosophy — kindness is global — and run karmacards.world alongside the table. They take table 158.

exhibitors.name: Halucha Hobbies
exhibitors.tagline: A double pitch in the middle block.
exhibitors.summary: Hobby dealer.
exhibitors.editorial: Halucha Hobbies take tables 134 and 135, a double pitch in the middle block. A general hobby dealer — the kind of table you dig through rather than target.

exhibitors.name: HarvboCards
exhibitors.tagline: The PSA desk on the floor.
exhibitors.summary: Macomb Twp., MI. An authorised PSA Elite Dealer running PSA and PSA/DNA group submissions.
exhibitors.editorial: Harvbo are a PSA Authorized Elite Dealer out of Macomb Township, running group submissions for PSA and PSA/DNA. At the 2026 National they processed 1,835 items for authentication and put through their largest ever PSA/DNA submission, over $35,000 of it. If you have grading questions, this is the table to bring them to.
take: An authorised PSA Elite Dealer out of Macomb Township, running group submissions for both PSA and PSA Autograph.

That makes this the table to visit if you are carrying raw cards you want graded. Bring the cards and the questions — group submissions are the cheapest route into PSA most collectors will find at a show.

exhibitors.name: Haus of Slabs
exhibitors.summary: Ultra-rare trading cards — DM to sell slabs.
exhibitors.editorial: Haus of Slabs deal at the rare end — 4,000 following built on ultra-rare trading cards, and an open invitation to send them slabs you want to sell. Associated with the Pop 1 card show. A table for people chasing the top of the print run.

exhibitors.name: Hidden Gems
exhibitors.tagline: Two tables, split across the block.
exhibitors.summary: Cards and collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: Hidden Gemz hold two tables, 31 and 40, split across the block rather than side by side — worth knowing if you find one and want to check the other.

exhibitors.name: Hitting Touchdowns
exhibitors.summary: Football cards.
exhibitors.editorial: Hitting Touchdowns is a football-focused table.

exhibitors.name: JMC Sports
exhibitors.summary: Downtown Lapeer — sports cards, autographed memorabilia and live breaks, heavy on Detroit and Michigan teams.
exhibitors.editorial: JMC run a shop in downtown Lapeer built around Detroit teams — Lions, Tigers, Red Wings, Pistons — plus Wolverines and Spartans, with autographed memorabilia and their own signing events. New releases, vintage wax and live breaks in the same room.

exhibitors.name: JSS Trading
exhibitors.tagline: First two tables past the door.
exhibitors.summary: Trading cards and collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: JSS Trading take tables 3 and 4 — the first pair past the entrance, which is the most-walked stretch of floor in the building.

exhibitors.name: Khanz Karz
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards.

exhibitors.name: Kresch Cards
exhibitors.tagline: Some live paycheck to paycheck. We live card to card.
exhibitors.summary: Adam Kresch — buying, selling and collecting, with a shop online.
exhibitors.editorial: Kresch Cards is Adam Kresch, 1,900 following and nearly 400 posts deep, with a line that tells you everything: some live paycheck to paycheck, we live card to card. Buying, selling and collecting, with an online store running alongside the shows.

exhibitors.name: Kruk Cards
exhibitors.tagline: A one-stop shop that has been buying for decades.
exhibitors.summary: A one-stop shop to buy or sell trading cards and collectibles, with a published buying line.
exhibitors.editorial: Kruk are an institution: 2,098 posts, a shop line on 248-656-8803, and a standing offer that runs from one card to an entire basement. They buy at shows and from collections, and they publish market thinking rather than only inventory.

exhibitors.name: Locked In Cards
exhibitors.summary: Card shows across Michigan — Pokémon slabs, singles and sealed.
exhibitors.editorial: Locked In work the Michigan show circuit rather than sitting still, carrying Pokémon slabs, singles and sealed. Dealers who travel restock constantly, so what is in the case at RazMania will not be what was in it a fortnight ago.
take: Michigan Pokémon dealer working the card-show circuit: slabs, singles and sealed, buy, sell and trade.
A show-circuit regular rather than a shopfront, which usually means sharper prices and a tighter, more curated case.

exhibitors.name: LT Legacy Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Sports trading cards.
exhibitors.editorial: LT Legacy take table 98, listed for sports trading cards. The Instagram handle given on their registration did not resolve, so the table is the place to find them.

exhibitors.name: Matcha Mew & Co.
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon and TCG.
exhibitors.editorial: Matcha Mew & Co. are a Pokémon and TCG table.

exhibitors.name: Meedo FC Cards
exhibitors.summary: Soccer cards all day, with inventory also listed on eBay.
exhibitors.editorial: Meedo is the soccer specialist here — a Select Euro 2020 Mbappé game-worn patch, Messi and Yamal, and an eBay store under the same name. A Watford supporter, which he will happily tell you about. If you collect soccer, this is the only table built entirely around it.

exhibitors.name: Michigan Card Collective
exhibitors.summary: Michigan Pokémon and TCG.
exhibitors.editorial: Michigan Card Collective are listed for Pokémon and TCG, and are one of the newer names on the Michigan circuit.

exhibitors.name: Miller's Sports Cards & Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards and memorabilia in Mount Pleasant — buy, sell and trade.
exhibitors.editorial: Miller's run a shop on North Mission Street in Mount Pleasant, buying, selling and trading sports cards and memorabilia with eBay storefronts running alongside. A mid-Michigan dealer at a Detroit-area show is worth a look, because different inventory travels in.

exhibitors.name: Mint Cards & Collectibles
exhibitors.tagline: Four friends, one Lake Orion shop.
exhibitors.summary: A family-run Lake Orion hobby shop — sports cards, Pokémon, One Piece, Magic, Lorcana, graded and sealed.
exhibitors.editorial: Mint was started by four lifelong friends — Simon Eisho, Marvin Shamwin, Donovan Mansour and Daved Putros — who grew up on cards and opened a shop in Lake Orion. They run trade nights and rip nights as much as they run a till, which tells you what kind of table to expect.

exhibitors.name: Mitchell's Landing
exhibitors.summary: Cards and collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: Mitchell's Landing bring a cards and collectibles table to both days.

exhibitors.name: MMD Cards
exhibitors.summary: One Piece and Pokémon, deep — cards, cards, cards.
exhibitors.editorial: MMD run One Piece and Pokémon across 716 posts and a YouTube channel, with three-thousand-follower giveaways to match. The tone is community first: they shout out other dealers by name more than they push their own stock, which is usually a good sign about a table.
take: One Piece and Pokémon, 700 posts deep, with a YouTube channel alongside the shop.
One Piece is the thinnest category on most Midwest floors, so if that is what you collect this is likely your only real stop.

exhibitors.name: Moodz Cards
exhibitors.summary: NBA and NFL out of Detroit — buying, selling and trading.
exhibitors.editorial: Moodz run NBA and NFL out of Detroit, with a personal collection built around the Pistons, Kevin Garnett, Joe Johnson and Luka Dončić. If you collect Detroit basketball, this is a table that will actually talk about it.

exhibitors.name: Moosemart TCG
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon, slabs and singles.
exhibitors.editorial: Moose Mart keep to Pokémon — slabs and singles, nothing else. A focused table for a single game.

exhibitors.name: Motor City Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade — Detroit Lions and Michigan State Spartans.
exhibitors.editorial: Motor City are exactly what the name suggests — Detroit Lions and Michigan State Spartans, bought, sold and traded by someone who follows both.

exhibitors.name: Motown Breaks
exhibitors.summary: Professional card cleaning and grading.
exhibitors.editorial: Motown Breaks do something almost nobody else on this floor does: professional card cleaning and grading prep. If you have a card you suspect would grade higher than it currently does, this is the table to put it in front of.

exhibitors.name: Motown Cards
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon and collectibles at low prices, out of Dearborn Heights.
exhibitors.editorial: Motown Cards run Pokémon and collectibles out of Dearborn Heights, and price is the pitch — they lead with low prices rather than grails. A good first stop if you are filling gaps in a set rather than chasing one specific card.

exhibitors.name: Muk Bang TCG
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade. Michigan card show vendor, trusted Pokémon dealer and creator of Slabdogs.
exhibitors.editorial: Muk Bang are a fixture on the Michigan card show circuit and describe themselves as a trusted Pokemon dealer, which in this hobby is a reputation you only get by pricing fairly for a long time. They also created Slabdogs.

exhibitors.name: One Team International Agency (OTIA)
exhibitors.summary: High-end sports cards and memorabilia, plus athlete appearances and private signings. Based outside Ann Arbor.
exhibitors.editorial: OTIA is Jason Koonce's business, and he has been brokering high-end cards and memorabilia for over twenty years — long enough to be profiled by PSA. Alongside the cards they arrange athlete and celebrity appearances and private signings, and they buy collections of any size, from a single card to a full room.

exhibitors.name: Orange Cards
exhibitors.summary: Sports and trading cards out of Metro Detroit, with an eBay storefront alongside.
exhibitors.editorial: Orange Cards run sports and trading cards out of Metro Detroit with close to 4,000 following, selling on eBay between shows. A local table with a national storefront behind it.

exhibitors.name: Pirate Hunter Deegs
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell and trade across Naruto, One Piece and Pokémon.
exhibitors.editorial: Deegs deal Naruto, One Piece and Pokémon, and publish their show schedule openly — RazMania is pinned in their bio next to the Michigan Toy and Comic Show. They come to this one straight off the Michigan Card Expo in Novi and the Detroit Card Show, which is a heavy August.

exhibitors.name: Pok_R_Us
exhibitors.summary: Lifelong collector turned vendor — sealed, singles, hits, mystery boxes and grab bags.
exhibitors.editorial: A lifelong collector turned vendor out of Michigan, running sealed, singles, hits, mystery boxes and grab bags. He gives product away about as often as he sells it — a Mega Feraligatr ex box went out in his first giveaway — and works the Michigan Card Expo circuit.
take: Verified Michigan Pokémon vendor running sealed, singles, hits, mystery boxes and grab bags.
Broad enough to cover a beginner and a chase-hunter at the same table, which is rarer than it sounds in the TCG corner of a show floor.

exhibitors.name: PokeDeals With Jake
exhibitors.tagline: Half the case is Riftbound now.
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon, Riftbound and Disney Lorcana — about half the case is Riftbound now.
exhibitors.editorial: Jake works the Michigan Pokémon show circuit, Lansing included, and posts from behind the table rather than in front of it. The mix has shifted since: roughly half the inventory is Riftbound now, with a lot of Disney Lorcana alongside it and some football coming for this weekend. Slab trades are the stated favourite.
take: Michigan Pokémon dealer working the show circuit.
Newer to Instagram than to the hobby — worth stopping by rather than judging by follower count.

exhibitors.name: PokeTom's Cards
exhibitors.summary: Fresh vendor trying to collect em all.
take: A newer Pokémon vendor, honest about being early in the journey.
New vendors are often where the underpriced singles are, precisely because they are still building a reputation.

exhibitors.name: Pokey Collector
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon collector and seller.
exhibitors.editorial: Pokey Collector sell and collect Pokémon, and lead with quality and service rather than volume — a deliberately small operation. Expect a curated case rather than long boxes, and a seller who can tell you where each card came from.

exhibitors.name: Profound Orthodontics
exhibitors.summary: Dr Justin Kammo's orthodontic practice, serving Oakland County since 2006.
exhibitors.editorial: Profound is Dr Justin Kammo's practice, running braces and Invisalign out of Bingham Farms, Northville and Southfield since 2006. They are backing RazMania as a partner rather than selling cards.

exhibitors.name: RCX Sports
exhibitors.summary: Bringing pro-league youth sports — NFL Flag, Jr NBA, NHL Street — to local communities.
exhibitors.editorial: RCX bring pro-league youth sports programmes to local communities: NFL Flag, Jr NBA, NHL Street and MLB Pitch Hit & Run. They are here as a partner, and worth a word if you have kids who would rather play than collect.

exhibitors.name: RIW Hobbies
exhibitors.summary: A Livonia games and hobby shop since 1998 — Pokémon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh, One Piece, Lorcana and Digimon.
exhibitors.editorial: RIW have been on Five Mile Road in Livonia since October 1998, named after the owner's late father, and they carry the 1,100-plus Google reviews that come with nearly three decades of doing it properly. Pokémon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh, One Piece, Lorcana and Digimon, plus the tournaments that turn a shop into a community.

exhibitors.name: Rob's Pop Shop
exhibitors.summary: Pops, prints and Pokémon.
exhibitors.editorial: Rob deals Funko Pops, prints and Pokémon, an unusual three-way that makes this the table to check if you collect outside cardboard. He is a fixture on the Michigan circuit, thanking the MI Card Expo and the Detroit Card Show in back-to-back posts.
take: Pops, prints and Pokémon — the clearest non-sports table on the floor.
If you are bringing kids, or you collect outside cardboard entirely, this is where to start.

exhibitors.name: Salmo Bros Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Rare grails and good vibes, brought to the local card show circuit.
exhibitors.editorial: Salmo Bros work the Michigan circuit — the Detroit Card Show and the new Motor City Card Fest both feature — and lead with rare grails and, in their words, the best vibes. Pokémon-heavy, and they pin their next show so you can find them between events.
take: A card-show regular that leans on grails and atmosphere in equal measure.
Check their pinned post before the show — they publish what they are bringing.

exhibitors.name: Sari Sari TCG
exhibitors.tagline: Pokémon and One Piece, Michigan crew.
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon and One Piece, bought, sold and traded — a Michigan crew.
exhibitors.editorial: Sari Sari are a Michigan-based Pokémon and One Piece table run by a crew rather than a single dealer, and they take table 189. Buy, sell and trade across both games.

exhibitors.name: Savage Scoops Gallery
exhibitors.summary: A resell store at 323 E 11 Mile Rd, Madison Heights, MI.
exhibitors.editorial: Savage Scoops run an actual storefront on East 11 Mile Road in Madison Heights. A resell store rather than a card-only table, which makes it one of the broader stops on the floor.

exhibitors.name: Sbisser161 Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Michigan sports cards — buy, sell and trade, from a veteran-owned table.
exhibitors.editorial: Sbisser161 is Shane Bissonette, an Army veteran running a Michigan sports card table. Buy, sell and trade across the board, with Michigan teams close to the centre of it — a table where the conversation tends to run longer than the transaction.

exhibitors.name: Scotty B Sports Cards
exhibitors.tagline: Card investing with the data attached.
exhibitors.summary: Sports card investing with the data attached — MLB rookies, PSA pops and market trends.
exhibitors.editorial: Scotty B approach cards as investing — tracking MLB rookies, PSA population reports and market trends, and publishing free reports on it.

exhibitors.name: Sebok Cards
exhibitors.tagline: Rookie patch autos and graded singles.
exhibitors.summary: Numbered rookie patch autos and PSA-graded singles across football, basketball and baseball.
exhibitors.editorial: Sebok deal at the top end of modern — National Treasures rookie patch autos numbered to 99, a Flawless Griffey auto numbered to 10, Panini Prizm and Select, much of it PSA graded. A table for people who already know which card they are looking for.

exhibitors.name: Secret Lair Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Crestwood's lair for collectibles and community, open Tuesday to Sunday.
exhibitors.editorial: Secret Lair calls itself Crestwood's lair for collectibles and community, and the hours back it up — open six days a week, Pokémon through memorabilia.
take: A Crestwood, Illinois shop built around community as much as inventory — open six days, with play space alongside the cases.
Pokémon, memorabilia and sports under one banner, so it covers more of a want list than a single-category table.

exhibitors.name: Showboat Breaks
exhibitors.summary: Detroit-based breaker, running live breaks on Whatnot.
exhibitors.editorial: Showboat runs live breaks out of Detroit on Whatnot. If you have never watched a break in person, this is the table to stand at.

exhibitors.name: Silverback Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Soccer, football and Disney Topps Chrome — always buying, selling and trading.
exhibitors.editorial: Silverback run an unusual three-lane table — soccer, football and Disney Topps Chrome — a combination you will not find twice on this floor. Always buying, selling and trading, and reachable by DM or email before the doors open.

exhibitors.name: Slabbed and Sold
exhibitors.summary: Buying, selling and trading cards — fair deals, fast shipping, trusted trader.
exhibitors.editorial: Slabbed and Sold trade on reputation — fair deals, fast shipping, and a trusted-trader record they maintain across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.

exhibitors.name: Snap City Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade.
exhibitors.editorial: Snap City lead with the three words that matter most at a show — buy, sell, trade — which means they are as interested in what you walk in carrying as what you walk out with. Worth a stop if you are bringing cards rather than only browsing.

exhibitors.name: SnapShot Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards.
exhibitors.editorial: SnapShot Sports Cards bring a sports card table to both days. Note their name is entered as 'Sorts' in the exhibitor list — a typo worth correcting.

exhibitors.name: Somerset
exhibitors.summary: Cards and collectibles.
exhibitors.editorial: Somerset bring a cards and collectibles table to both days.

exhibitors.name: Sport Card Locker HQ
exhibitors.summary: A show-circuit regular working Detroit, Chicago, Minnesota and Indiana.
exhibitors.editorial: Sport Card Locker travel further than most — Detroit Sports Spectacular, Chicago Sports Spectacular, the Minnesota card show and Miller Card Fest in Noblesville all turn up in their feed. Inventory that moves through that many rooms is usually worth a look.

exhibitors.name: Sports card one
exhibitors.summary: Always buying, selling and trading all sports cards, modern and vintage era.
take: Modern and vintage across all sports, buying and selling both.
A generalist table, which is exactly what you want when your want list crosses eras.

exhibitors.name: SportsKid Podcast
exhibitors.tagline: A kid, his dad, and Detroit sports.
exhibitors.summary: Detroit sports commentary, cards and memorabilia — hosted by a kid and his dad.
exhibitors.editorial: SportsKid is Detroit sports commentary, cards and memorabilia hosted by a kid and his dad. Bring your own kid to this table.

exhibitors.name: ST Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Steve and Tyler — cards, jerseys and memorabilia, all available to trade or buy.
exhibitors.editorial: ST is Steve and Tyler, running cards, jerseys and memorabilia with everything on the table open to trade as well as sale. Boston based, so the inventory skews differently from the Michigan tables around them.

exhibitors.name: Stoney Sports Vault
exhibitors.tagline: Real deals, filmed on the road.
exhibitors.summary: Real sports card deals, real negotiations, real stories from the road. Buying, selling and trading.
exhibitors.editorial: Stoney films the hobby as much as he sells it — real negotiations and stories from the road, with a new video every week and four thousand following along. Recent posts come from The National and Columbus Card Fest, which is the circuit this table has been working all summer.
take: Verified, nearly 4,000 followers, and a YouTube channel built on filming the actual negotiations rather than just the pulls.
A dealer who publishes their deal-making tends to price consistently, because the footage is the reputation. Expect to be able to talk numbers.

exhibitors.name: Suga Sports Cards
exhibitors.summary: Michigan-based, always buying, selling and trading across every sport.
exhibitors.editorial: Suga cover every sport rather than specialising, are Michigan based, and say the DMs are always open. A good table to bring a mixed lot to.

exhibitors.name: The Card Cave MI
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade. Store hours Tuesday–Sunday 12–8. 8242 23 Mile Rd, Shelby Twp.
take: A Shelby Township storefront that opened in July, open seven days a week noon to eight.
New shops tend to arrive at shows with fresh inventory and something to prove. Worth a look early in the day.

exhibitors.name: The Kanto Emporium
exhibitors.tagline: Custom prints and displays, made to order.
exhibitors.summary: Custom prints, displays and TCG — built to order.
exhibitors.editorial: Kanto Emporium do something most of the floor does not — custom prints and displays alongside the TCG, with an open invitation to bring them an idea and have it made. If you have wanted a card or a set displayed properly, this is the table to describe it at.

exhibitors.name: The Mewseum
exhibitors.summary: A collection built entirely around Mew and Mewtwo.
exhibitors.editorial: The Mewseum is exactly what it sounds like — a collection built entirely around Mew and Mewtwo, run out of New Jersey. If you collect one Pokémon line seriously, this is the table that will understand why.

exhibitors.name: The Two Point Show
exhibitors.tagline: Weekly sports news, live from the floor.
exhibitors.summary: A weekly sports news show from Joey Klott and Gidja Beers, on Instagram and YouTube.
exhibitors.editorial: The Two Point Show is Joey Klott and Gidja Beers putting out weekly sports news across Instagram and YouTube, with a proper crew behind it — their own graphic designer and editor. They are at RazMania as media rather than as a dealer, so expect a microphone rather than a display case.

exhibitors.name: Thunder Vault Collectibles
exhibitors.tagline: The most electrifying Pokémon vendor on Instagram.
exhibitors.summary: In their own words, the most electrifying Pokémon TCG vendor on Instagram.
exhibitors.editorial: Thunder Vault describe themselves as the most electrifying Pokémon TCG vendor on Instagram, and with 67 posts behind the claim they are committed to it. A straight Pokémon table.

exhibitors.name: Tri-Covery
exhibitors.summary: Massage, assisted stretching and recovery — the first of its kind in Michigan.
exhibitors.editorial: Tri-Covery was founded by Jeff Kong, a trainer and massage therapist who reckoned recovery was the missing piece of most training programmes. They combine massage, assisted stretching and corrective exercise out of Novi, with an unusual concentration of Fascial Stretch Therapy trained therapists. A partner rather than a dealer — and worth knowing about after two days on a hard floor.

exhibitors.name: Turkish Breaks
exhibitors.summary: Buying and selling singles, plus a cleaning and grading service. Based in Michigan.
exhibitors.editorial: Turkish Breaks do the thing most breakers do not — they also clean and grade. Buying and selling singles alongside it, out of Michigan.

exhibitors.name: Underdog Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Always bet on the underdog — 2,400 posts and 5,000 following.
exhibitors.editorial: Underdog carry the largest following of any recent addition — 5,000 on Instagram across 2,400 posts, trading under #AlwaysBetOnTheUnderdog. A collectibles store with a long track record behind the table.

exhibitors.name: Victory Cards and Collectibles
exhibitors.summary: Michigan-based — buy, sell and trade across all sports cards and memorabilia.
exhibitors.editorial: Victory are a newer Michigan table covering sports cards and memorabilia across the board, buying, selling and trading. Early enough in their run that the case changes a lot between shows, so it is worth a look even if you saw them last month.

exhibitors.name: VTM Vending
exhibitors.summary: Smart vending machines built in Cleveland — and yes, they vend trading cards.
exhibitors.editorial: VTM build smart vending machines in Cleveland and run them in over 1,500 locations across all 50 states, at a $20M annualised run rate. The reason they matter on this floor: their machines vend Pokémon and baseball cards alongside everything else, with age-verification scanners built in. Worth a look if you have ever wondered what a card vending machine actually costs.

exhibitors.name: Wolf Hearts Cards
exhibitors.summary: Buy, sell, trade, collect. Established 2024, and a dealer for Slabmags.
exhibitors.editorial: Wolf Hearts have been at it since 2024 and are a dealer for Slabmags. Buy, sell, trade, collect — in that order.

exhibitors.name: WRLD of Cards
exhibitors.summary: Pokémon singles, slabs and sealed always in stock. Based in south-east Michigan.
exhibitors.editorial: WRLD of Cards keep Pokemon singles, slabs and sealed in stock at all times, out of south-east Michigan, and they are always open to a trade.

exhibitors.name: Y.G.'s Card Vault
exhibitors.tagline: Sports and TCG under one roof.
exhibitors.summary: Dealers in both sports cards and TCG.
exhibitors.editorial: Y.G.'s Card Vault deal in both sports cards and TCG, a wider spread than most of the single-focus tables around them.

exhibitors.name: Z's Sports House of Cards
exhibitors.summary: Sports cards, straight up — buy, sell, trade, with an eBay storefront behind it.
exhibitors.editorial: Z's carry the largest Instagram following on this floor at over 5,600, running sports across buy, sell and trade, and selling through eBay as Zezula Sports Cards between shows. A Detroit Card Show regular.
